Definition: properly, to wound; but only figuratively, to taunt or insult
BiblicalUsage: Kalam is the wound of words — to taunt, to insult, to put to shame. David's men tell Nabal's shepherds they were not hurt by them; the servants of Saul say the men were very good unto us and we were not hurt; and Ezra says he is ashamed and blushes to lift up his face to God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word shows that shame is a wound too, and words can inflict it. David's men did not hurt Nabal's shepherds, and Ezra felt the hurt of his people's sin — and that is why I want my words to heal rather than wound.
